title: FNIH Awards
bodyHtml:
FNIH-funded investigators, 2022 - 2025

  1. Johan LM Björkegren (Karolinska Institute, Sweden and Mt. Sinai) and Panos Roussos (Mt. Sinai)

    "STARNET (the Stockholm-Tartu Atherosclerosis Reverse Network Engineering Task) – a multi-tissue omics resource of living patients with cardiometabolic disease (CMD) and coronary artery disease (CAD)"

    The STARNET project will share existing bulk (e.g. DNA, RNA) and generate new snATAC-seq and snRNA-seq data from up to 7 tissues isolated from up to 1400 living CMD patients with CAD and from 400 CAD-free controls to: (1) identify molecular mechanisms within and across metabolically relevant organs responsible for the development of CMDs; and (2) examine how these CMDs drive the progression of CAD/atherosclerosis.

  2. Alisa Manning (Broad Institute)

    “Common metabolic disease genetic association analysis in the All of Us Research Program”

    Project will generate and discover novel genetic associations with GWAS using electronic health records (up to 214K subjects) and CMD-related circulating and imaging biomarkers (up to 329K subjects) in the All of Us Research Program.

  3. Bing Ren and Kyle Gaulton (UCSD)

    “Comprehensive single cell multiomic profiling of the human heart in control and disease”

    Project will identify variants, regulatory programs and genes involved in heart failure by performing single cell multiomic analysis of all chambers in 30 human hearts from control and ischemic or non-ischemic heart failure subjects including diabetics.

  4. Bing Ren, Kyle Gaulton, and Tatiana Kisseleva (UCSD)

    “Comprehensive single cell multiomic profiling of the human liver in control and disease”

    Project will identify variants, regulatory programs and genes involved in liver disease by performing single cell multiomic analysis of 85 human liver samples from normal, NAFL or NASH subjects.

  5. Laura Scott (U. Michigan) and Karen Mohlke (UNC)

    “Single nucleus RNA-seq and metabolomics in subcutaneous adipose tissue”

    The project will identify associations in subcutaneous adipose tissue between CMD traits and cell type single nucleus gene expression and cell type proportions as well as associations between cell type single nucleus gene expression and genetic variants using single nucleus RNA-seq from up to 646 individuals from the METSIM and FUSION studies, and identify metabolites associated with CMD phenotypes and genetic variants in up to 806 METSIM individuals.

  6. Kerrin Small (King’s College London)

    “Adipose tissue Multi-omics in TwinsUK”

    Project will provide a comprehensive resource of adipose molecular profile associations in approximately 800 twin subjects in the TwinsUK cohort, including an aging population by integrating matched adipose omics datasets with genetic and clinical phenotype data.
